recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-15808; any future valueset-supplement context or behavior work belongs in the FHIR Extension Pack, where the related FHIR-40761 work is already reflected in current source.
issue_request: Published STU3 Vocab change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking that extension values targeting canonical infrastructure or knowledge resources such as CodeSystem and ValueSet use canonical(...) rather than Reference(...).
initial_application: Applied by svn revision 15373 / git commit caade7d22f6ac69282b179c5f488a1fa2a799d53, which changed historical extension spreadsheet rows including valueset-system and valueset-supplement from Reference(CodeSystem) to canonical(CodeSystem), and valueset-map from Reference(ConceptMap) to canonical(ConceptMap).
additional_context: The old core ValueSet extension spreadsheet is no longer active in the current core build. Current source/fhir.ini lists active core extension/profile spreadsheets without a ValueSet-specific extension spreadsheet. The valueset-supplement extension now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack and its current StructureDefinition uses canonical(CodeSystem); later FHIR-40761 context additions are also present there. The only current core structured XML Reference(ValueSet) hits found were EvidenceVariable resource elements, not extension definitions, so they are outside the final resolution scope.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current core extension spreadsheets contain no Reference(CodeSystem), Reference(ValueSet), or Reference(ConceptMap) type strings, and the moved valueset-supplement definition is already canonical(CodeSystem).

related_jiras.note: Later retracted request for an $expand supplement parameter; it does not alter FHIR-15808 canonical type handling.
FHIR-extensions issue adding ValueSet.compose.include/exclude contexts for valueset-supplement; current Extension Pack source includes these contexts and remains canonical(CodeSystem).
